subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Should OpenClaw solve this tool-result cache problem by preserving current-turn observations and only compacting stale or heartbeat-specific results, or by adopting provider-level placeholders for selected tool results?
rationale: The choice changes model-visible tool-result semantics and provider-cache behavior; code inspection can identify unsafe cases, but maintainers must choose the long-term visibility policy before a broad result-redaction fix lands.

options.title: Preserve fresh observations
options.body: Keep current-turn `read`, `exec`, search, and memory results visible to the model, and restrict any cache-oriented summaries to stale-history or heartbeat-only paths with tests and live proof.

options.title: Adopt explicit placeholders
options.body: Allow provider-level placeholders only for a maintainer-approved narrow tool set whose results are proven not to be needed for follow-up reasoning.

options.title: Defer to broader cache strategy
options.body: Pause this branch if the preferred solution is the live-proven boundary-aware cache strategy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95311 or heartbeat isolation rather than result redaction.

recommendation.title: Preserve fresh observations
recommendation.body: Keep current-turn `read`, `exec`, search, and memory results visible to the model, and restrict any cache-oriented summaries to stale-history or heartbeat-only paths with tests and live proof.
